medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of Absence are granted on written request for reasons of academic difficulty, personal or health problems, or for an educational purpose. Leaves are generally granted for one year, with an extension under special circumstances. Leaves of Absence for more than two years or a second Leave of Absence for the same set of reasons are generally not granted.  A rare exception to this could be made by the Dean for Students for reasons of disability, serious illness, or other personal hardship. When necessary, a Board may impose a Leave of Absence for academic difficulty or inability to meet any School of Medicine Technical Standards, with approval by the Dean.  For the full policy on Leaves of Absence, refer to the NYU School of Medicine Student Handbook, which is available to all medical students at http://school.med.nyu.edu/studentsfaculty/student-affairs/student-resources/student-handbook .
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The NYU Grossman School of Medicine has a rich history of extra-curricular involvement. Students elect to be involved in one or more of our 80+ student-formed organizations. Some of these are for fun, while others address career or academic topics with larger, complex issues. We have something for everyone, and if students do not see an organization that interests them, there is always room to create one that does. Formed by elected members of the Student Body, the School of Medicine Student Council serves as the official representative body for School of Medicine students and student organizations.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: NYU Grossman School of Medicine lies at the heart of midtown Manhattan in New York City and at the center of the NYU Langone Health complex, which includes the Kimmel Pavilion, Hassenfeld Children's Hospital, Tisch University Hospital, NYU Cancer Center, Rusk Institute for Rehabilitation Medicine, NYU Langone Orthopedic Hospital, NYU Langone Brooklyn Hospital and NYU's major hospital affiliates, Bellevue Hospital and the Manhattan VA Hospital. This is in addition to numerous surrounding outpatient centers in the five boroughs and greater tri-state area.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: All single students are guaranteed housing in Vilcek Hall (334 East 26th Street).  In this residential building for medical students, there is 24-hour security staffing and card-swipe access.  Housing information for incoming medical students can be found on their website at https://med.nyu.edu/our-community/life-nyu-grossman-school-medicine/housing/md-md/phd-student-housing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:

medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The mission of the Wellness Programs at NYUGSOM is to create spaces for students to engage in the 8 components of wellness (emotional, physical, financial, environmental, occupational, spiritual, intellectual, social) through initiatives that empower personal autonomy by providing choices of wellness activity to engage in, help students feel more competent in their roles as future physicians, and encourage a stronger sense of community, where we uplift one another and cultivate a culture of compassion and wellness at NYUGSOM.

We understand that wellness and wellness practices are not a one size fits all, and that wellness can encompass anything from emotional health, to structural issues. With that in mind, we approach wellness with various offerings—both curricular and non-curricular— to support students during their training. There are 7 sessions of carved out curricular time for wellness. These sessions take place during key transition points in your training in the curriculum that we use as a way to introduce evidence-based tools that can support your well-being. Our para-curricular offerings include a 5-week Mind-Body skills class that helps teach students how to tap into their bodies to enhance emotional regulation especially during high stress moments. 

We have two different wellness-oriented student groups on campus: the Wellness curriculum committee and Student wellness committee. The Wellness Curriculum Committee meets to discuss ways we can improve or innovate on our curricular wellness programming. The Student Wellness Committee supports the physical, emotional and mental wellbeing of students so that you don't just survive but thrive throughout medical school and beyond.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At NYU Grossman School of Medicine, we strive to recruit and accept an academically talented and interpersonally gifted student body with the collective ability and desire to deliver excellence in clinical care, research, and medical education to all members of society. The admissions committee strives to identify applicants we believe are poised to become tomorrow’s physician leaders. We are interested in applicants who are committed to meeting the needs of our patients, community, and the medical profession at large, as well as those prepared to thrive in our culture of excellence.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: We expect our students to dress in a professional manner.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty are available to meet outside of class to review and discuss course material with students.  In addition, each content director arranges for tutoring sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: M1 students have clinical experiences starting their first week. M2 students have core clerkship rotations. M2 and M3 students have subinternships, critical care rotations, and elective rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, Labs, Case-based instruction; Small Group Discussion; Team-Based Learning; Flipped Classrooms; Individual Learning
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: We do not rank our students.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is expected but not mandated at most lectures; lectures are recorded and can be viewed asynchronously. Some lectures and educational events are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
NYU Grossman School of Medicine trains future physicians with an innovative, flexible Three-Year MD degree curriculum known as the Curriculum for the 21st Century Personalized Pathways, or C21. Our curriculum enables students to master the skills necessary to succeed in medicine in three years, and provides opportunities to customize their studies at designated points in their training. The first stage of the curriculum is a one-year pre-clerkship period of instruction, with clerkships beginning at the start of the second year. While we integrate opportunities for career exploration throughout each medical school, year, this will be further honed in the post-clerkship year(s), with the opportunity to participate in advanced research, electives or selectives; ultimately, the NYUGSOM experience allows for the development of expertise in any desired area of interest.

C21 offers unparalleled flexibility, allowing students to graduate in either 3 or 4 years, including a variety of four-year dual degree options and dedicated research years added to the standard three-year MD curriculum. We are also the first school in the country to offer an accelerated Three-Year MD Pathway that provides direct progression into any of our residency programs pending successful completion of your medical school training. 

https://med.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/md-curriculum/
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
NYU Grossman School of Medicine's Foundational Clinical Skills (FCS) module runs parallel to the rest of the pre-clerkship curriculum and focuses on the skills of doctoring. Students learn about prevention, health care systems, and psychosocial issues along with core interviewing skills, physical diagnosis and clinical epidemiology. FCS specifically presents material on interdisciplinary teamwork. 

The required ambulatory care clerkship has a series of didactic lectures, OSCE and practice in ambulatory clinics to enrich our students' exposure to primary care medicine. In addition, the Department of Medicine offers a summer honors program that supports primary care oriented research.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: All students participate in substantive research with world-class NYU Langone Health scientists and laboratories.  Students have a plethora of opportunities to carry out medically relevant research throughout their time at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, starting with their first year of medical school.  Students typically choose to pursue original, hypothesis-driven research in the basic, clinical, or translational sciences. All students participate in established Summer Research Fellowships (SRFs) between M1 and M2 years and continue research in later years, culminating in the completion of a scholarly product.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Though not required, community service is extremely important for our students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: All medical students must complete an Area of Concentration consisting of 2 core research experiences, a 6 week Summer Research Fellowship (SRF) between stage 1 and 2 & a stage 3 scholarly project.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1841, NYU Grossman School of Medicine is one of the nation's preeminent medical schools. For over 180 years, we have trained thousands of physicians who have enriched countless lives and helped shape medical history. Located in the heart of New York City, our students benefit from training at nine state-of-the-art hospitals in Manhattan and Brooklyn, Bellevue Hospital, and the Manhattan VA. We pride ourselves on providing students with unparalleled curricular flexibility, including the country's first Three-Year MD Pathway with direct progression into any one of our residency programs. Our C21 Personalized Pathways Curriculum provides a one-year preclerkship experience with clerkships throughout the second year, and a plethora of four year dual degree options.  We offer every one of our MD students with Tuition-Free Scholarships, alongside Debt-Free scholarships for those who qualify to meet 100% of an individual's demonstrated financial need with scholarships.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: At NYU Grossman School of Medicine, we strive to recruit and accept the most academically talented and interpersonally gifted student body, one with a collective ability and desire to deliver excellence in clinical care, research, and medical education to all members of society. The admissions committee strives to identify applicants we believe are poised to become tomorrow’s physician leaders. We are interested in applicants who are committed to meeting the needs of our patients, community, and the medical profession at large, as well as those prepared to thrive in our culture of excellence.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: NYU Grossman School of Medicine has technical standards that describe the essential abilities and qualities required for matriculation, progression, and graduation. Students must be able, with or without reasonable accommodations, to meet standards in six domains: behavioral and social attributes; communication; ethics and professionalism; intellectual–conceptual, integrative, and quantitative abilities; motor; and observation. These standards reflect essential program requirements and patient safety needs and are applied in a manner consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Rehabilitation Act. NYUGSOM provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities through the Moses Center for Student Accessibility. Applicants invited to interview acknowledge they have reviewed the technical standards; enrolled students attest annually that they can meet these standards with or without accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
NYU Grossman School of Medicine is dedicated to providing world-class education and improving affordability for all our students. We offer yearly Tuition-Free Scholarships to all full-time enrolled MD students taking required coursework towards their MD degree, assuming they are performing satisfactorily academically and professionally. This scholarship fully covers the cost of tuition for each of the three years the student spends at NYU Grossman School of Medicine towards their MD Degree. For the 2025-2026 academic cycle, every MD student received at least a $64,250 Tuition-Free Scholarship, fully offsetting the tuition charge and resulting in a net cost of attendance for an M1 student of $35,258. These Tuition-Free Scholarships are need-blind, are automatically provided to all our MD students, and effectively make the school tuition-free. 

Our full-time enrolled MD students can also apply for need-based Debt-Free Scholarships to help cover some or all of the remaining cost of living expenses, such as housing, food, books, and other miscellaneous items. These scholarships allow us to meet 100% of the demonstrated need for our MD students who qualify. We also provide a limited number of full-cost attendance scholarships in addition to our Tuition-Free and need-based Debt-Free Scholarships.   Thanks to our incredibly robust financial aid packages and synergies arising from our Three-Year MD C21 Curriculum, approximately 80% of recent graduates have graduated without medical educational debt.

For more information, see https://med.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/md-affordability-financial-aid/cost-attendance

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: NYU Grossman School of Medicine's accelerated C21 Personalized Pathways Curriculum enables our students to earn their MD degree in 3 years, fast-tracking their entry into medicine. They may also enter our Directed Residency Pathway for direct progression to any of our NYU Langone Health residency programs after this three-year MD curriculum. Alternatively, students may opt to pursue a dedicated research year or dual degree alongside their MD, in a total of four years.
medSchoolMdPathway.spotAvailable: All 102 students annually enter this accelerated three-year C21 Curriculum. They may (1) enter residency programs nationwide after this three-year track, (2) pursue a research year or dual degree for a four-year track, or (3) apply to the Directed Residency Pathway, which guarantees placement in an NYULH residency after three years; 41 spots are available each year for this Directed Residency Pathway.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: All matriculated NYUGSOM medical students undergo our Three-Year C21 MD Curriculum.  All NYUGSOM medical students are eligible to apply, either during their application cycle to medical school or during their second year of medical school, to our Directed Residency Pathway.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Application deadlines are the same as those listed above in the MSAR for medical school admission.  If applying to the Directed Pathway as an applicant or as an M2 student, a tertiary application is completed by the end of January of that cycle (i.e., January of their application year, or January of their M2 year).
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Completion of a tertiary application in addition to an AMCAS primary and NYUGSOM secondary app is required.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option available to Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants typically are notified of their waitlist status in mid-January.  Applicants can be accepted from the waitlist up until the first day of orientation in July.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: NYU Grossman School of Medicine has no required prerequisite courses.  We do, however, recommend coursework in the following:  Introductory Biology w/lab, Inorganic Chemistry w/lab, Organic Chemistry w/lab, Physics w/lab, Biochemistry, English, Genetics, Statistics, Psychology and Sociology.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Courses should be taken within five years of desired matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: At NYU Grossman School of Medicine, we strive to recruit and accept the most academically talented and interpersonally gifted student body, one with a collective ability and desire to deliver excellence in clinical care, research, and medical education to all members of society.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: NYU Grossman School of Medicine does not require shadowing.  That said, some shadowing is recommended to confirm to yourself that the medical profession is your ideal career path.
